problem: Given that $L{{t}^{n}}=\frac{n!}{{s}^{n+1}},$ find the Laplace transform $L{{e}^{4t}\cdot {t}^{3}}.$

activity_context.topic_title: The First Shifting Theorem of Laplace Transforms

feedback.problem: Given that $L{\operatorname{cos}⁡(\omega t)}=\frac{s}{{s}^{2}+{\omega }^{2}},$ find the Laplace transform $L{{e}^{-3t}\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡(6t)}.$
feedback.worked_solution:
The first shifting theorem states that if
$L{f(t)}=F(s),$
then
$L{{e}^{at}f(t)}=F(s-a).$

Using the given result, we have

$$
L{\operatorname{cos}⁡(6t)}=\frac{s}{{s}^{2}+{6}^{2}}.
$$

Therefore, applying the first shifting theorem, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}L{{e}^{-3t}\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡(6t)} & =\frac{s+3}{(s+3)^{2}+{6}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{s+3}{(s+3)^{2}+36}.\end{aligned}
$$
